starter_1.name: Dawn at the Sphinx
starter_1.description: The Great Sphinx, and the writing at its feet that nobody alive can read. The map says start here.

starter_2.name: Papyrus Merchant's Route
starter_2.description: Papyrus went up the Nile by this road, and the merchants wrote down who owed what. The receipts outlasted the cargo.

starter_3.name: Temple of Bastet
starter_3.description: Bastet's temple. The cats here were sacred, and the yearly festival was the biggest in Egypt — boats, music, the lot.

starter_4.name: Scribe's Academy
starter_4.description: The scribes' school. They cut their hieroglyphs into broken pottery, because papyrus was far too dear for children.

starter_treasure_tomb.name: Forgotten Merchant's Cache
starter_treasure_tomb.description: A merchant's cellar, not a king's: jars stacked, sealed and labelled, and nobody down there to argue about them.
starter_treasure_tomb.mapHint: The scrap sketches a market road and a cellar door — a trader's hiding place, nothing grander.

junior_1.name: Sacred Ibis Migration
junior_1.description: Marsh country, and the ibis wading through it. Egypt watched these birds: when they come back, the flood is coming.

junior_2.name: Valley of the Artisans
junior_2.description: Deir el-Medina, where the tomb-makers lived. Everything that went into a royal burial was made here first, in moulds.

junior_3.name: Temple of Thoth
junior_3.description: Thoth's temple. He invented writing, kept the records and did the counting — which is most of what we have been doing.

junior_4.name: Lighthouse of Alexandria
junior_4.description: The Pharos of Alexandria. A fire at the top, burning all night, and sailors finding the coast a day's sail out.

junior_treasure_tomb.name: Noble's Hidden Vault
junior_treasure_tomb.description: A noblewoman's vault, painted floor to ceiling. She bought the finest copies money could buy, and never once said so.
junior_treasure_tomb.mapHint: Fine ink, a crested seal in the corner — someone of standing wanted this room forgotten.

expert_1.name: Valley of the Kings
expert_1.description: The Valley of the Kings. They stopped building pyramids and hid the royal tombs in one valley, under a peak shaped like one.

expert_2.name: Karnak Temple Complex
expert_2.description: Karnak, added to for two thousand years. The great hall alone has a hundred and thirty-four columns, every one of them carved.

expert_3.name: Nile Delta Expedition
expert_3.description: Where the Nile splits and spreads out green. Sobek's country — papyrus, fish, and crocodiles that were worshipped and fed.

expert_4.name: Pyramid of Djoser
expert_4.description: Djoser's step pyramid, the first thing of its size built in stone. His architect Imhotep ended up remembered as a god.

expert_treasure_tomb.name: High Priest's Treasury
expert_treasure_tomb.description: A high priest's treasury, under the offering floor. Everything down there was given to a god and never taken out again.
expert_treasure_tomb.mapHint: The lines trace a temple precinct, and a stair running down beneath its offering floor.

expert_treasure_tomb_b.name: Inner Sanctum
expert_treasure_tomb_b.description: The sealed room at the heart of the temple. The high priest went in once a day, to wash the god and dress him.
expert_treasure_tomb_b.mapHint: Corridors run past the temple vaults to a sealed door — only the highest priests ever passed it.

master_1.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
master_1.description: The Great Pyramid. Twenty years of stone, and a whole town beside it feeding the crews on bread and beer.

master_2.name: Book of the Dead
master_2.description: Not one book but a set of spells, copied to order. The cheaper ones left a blank where your name should go.

master_3.name: Curse of the Pharaohs
master_3.description: The famous curse was invented by newspapers in 1923. The Egyptians guarded their tombs with doors and paperwork.

master_4.name: Tomb of Nefertari
master_4.description: Nefertari's tomb, the best-painted room in Egypt. The colours were ground from stone — azurite, malachite, ochre.

master_treasure_tomb.name: Pharaoh's Secret Hoard
master_treasure_tomb.description: A king's private hoard, out where the maps give up. Whatever went into the ground with him is still down there.
master_treasure_tomb.mapHint: A royal cartouche marks one edge, and the route ends far out under open sand.

master_treasure_tomb_b.name: Hall of Osiris
master_treasure_tomb_b.description: Osiris's hall. God of the flood and the grain — whatever goes under the ground here is expected back.
master_treasure_tomb_b.mapHint: Below the royal chambers the map keeps descending, into a hall marked with the rites of the dead.

wizard_1.name: Ra's Solar Journey
wizard_1.description: Ra goes under the world at sunset and has twelve hours of dark to cross. Egypt wrote down what happens in each one.

wizard_2.name: Colossi of Memnon
wizard_2.description: Two seated giants of Amenhotep III. The Greeks decided they were somebody else, and that name stuck for two thousand years.

wizard_3.name: Chamber of Ma'at
wizard_3.description: Ma'at's chamber. She is the order of things, and her single ostrich feather is what everything else gets measured against.

wizard_4.name: Eternal Pyramid
wizard_4.description: The casing was polished limestone, white as salt, dressed so exactly you could see it flash from a day's walk away.

wizard_treasure_tomb.name: Vault of the Gods
wizard_treasure_tomb.description: Where the temple kept what belonged to the gods. Nobody was announced in here without the right thing in their hands.
wizard_treasure_tomb.mapHint: No landmark on this scrap belongs to the mortal world — whatever it charts, gods put it there.

wizard_treasure_tomb_b.name: Realm of Cosmic Forces
wizard_treasure_tomb_b.description: Star charts across the ceiling, painted so the dead could tell the hour at night. Somebody's rope still hangs in the shaft.
wizard_treasure_tomb_b.mapHint: Past the divine vault the lines break into star-paths, where the forces of life and chaos are kept as relics.

wizard_treasure_tomb_c.name: Throne of Eternity
wizard_treasure_tomb_c.description: One seat at the centre and forty-two judges around it, each one asking a question you are supposed to answer no to.
wizard_treasure_tomb_c.mapHint: Every star-path on this fragment converges on a single seat at the very heart of the divine realm.

dev_topology.name: Topology Proving Ground
dev_topology.description: One site per floor-topology feature. Develop mode only.
